title: QC decisions must be atomic, provenance-bearing, append-only, and race-guarded
requirement: A QC/review decision on a queue item MUST be recorded as an atomic, append-only record carrying a full provenance snapshot (what was decided, on what evidence, by whom/when), kept distinguishable from mutation of the item's own live operational record. Two concurrent decisions on the same item MUST NOT both succeed as independent writes: the collision MUST be caught (e.g. by a uniqueness constraint) and resolved as a rejection, a no-op, or an explicit correction — never a silent duplicate, a crash, or lost data.
rationale: This is not one copied pattern but two independently-originated lineages converging on the same contract. Watch-clank (the fleet's original reference) implements it as a separate TABLE (event_reviews) in the same database with a unique constraint and documented IntegrityError-as-correction handling, explicitly grounded in a named incident: 'Built 2026-08-18 in response to the Citizen stale/out-of-stock flood autopsy.' Chinese-tech-wire, independently, implements it as a separate SQLite FILE (qc_archive.db) with its own unique constraint and its own stated rationale (archive durability against pipeline rebuilds). Every other surveyed Clank with a QC screen (korean-tech-wire, oem-radar, semiconductor-intelligence, smartwatch-clank, feature-phone-clank, tablet-clank) implements the same underlying contract, in one or the other physical shape. The physical shape (table vs. file) differs and is deliberately NOT part of this requirement, per decisions/0001-standardise-contracts-not-implementation.md.
forbidden: Writing a QC decision as a plain UPDATE/INSERT into the item's own live record with no separate decision record
A QC write path with no uniqueness constraint or equivalent collision guard
Treating a race as an unhandled exception surfaced to the operator as a crash
acceptance: A decision record exists that is distinct from the item's live/operational row, with enough fields to reconstruct what was decided and why
A DB-level or equivalent uniqueness constraint exists on (item id) for the decision record
A concurrent second decision attempt is demonstrably handled (test or code path) as a rejection/no-op/correction, not a crash or silent duplicate

evidence.summary: Built 2026-08-18 in direct response to a named incident: 'the Citizen stale/out-of-stock flood autopsy.'
event_reviews table, unique constraint uq_event_review_event_id, documented IntegrityError-as-correction handling.
Independently-originated separate-file archive with its own stated rationale and explicit SQLite-serialization argument for why the race is closed.

Same contract re-implemented (mostly via a copied/derived lineage) in every other surveyed Clank with a QC screen; semiconductor-intelligence's version explicitly mirrors watch-clank's contract, not the file-based lineage.

Counter-evidence / negative case: the one Clank whose QC action (CLI qc-action) is a raw INSERT into the live analyst_actions table, with no separate archive, no uniqueness constraint, and no documented race handling — exactly the anti-pattern this standard forbids.

notes: Pass 1 candidate. smartphone-clank's current qc-action implementation would not conform if this is ratified as-is; that is flagged as an open remediation/exception question in docs/gui-ratification-pass-1.md, not resolved here.
